title: Perfect point complex
statement:
In the Poincare duality conventions [def-pod-conventions] of this chapter (the fixed setting), an
object $C$ of the
category at the point [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point] is
*perfect* if it is quasi-isomorphic to a bounded complex of finite
projective $A$-modules [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex]. The *derived dual* is
$C^\vee=R\operatorname{Hom}_A(C,A)$, and the canonical evaluation and
coevaluation are the maps of the tensor–internal-Hom adjunction.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q98-c68271550 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read in full the item, both blueprint texts, the four cited nodes (with blueprint_update), Stacks more-algebra.tex l.18871 (Tag 0657 definition-perfect) and the unit and chapter records. The delivery is a definition-only split with no new nodes. The statement is main-20261015 order 2587 verbatim with inline citations added; master 2243 differs only by the missing article. Each clause matches its source: the setting and C^vee=RHom_A(C,A) come from def-pod-conventions, the point categories from def-weil-finite-coefficient-point, and the perfectness clause is def-pc-perfect-ring-complex with R=A, which agrees with Stacks 0657. The evaluation and coevaluation clause is adjunction data only and claims no exact pairing. Nothing is weakened, and no properness or smoothness is added. Small cases: A_{E,1}, O_E (a DVR) and E make every object perfect. A_{E,2} does not: A/varpi has nonzero Tor_i(A/varpi,A/varpi) for all i, so it is not perfect and the condition is genuine. The zero complex and A[0] are perfect. The Qbar_l stage has to be read stagewise through the 2-colimit; that reading comes from the blueprint convention, not from the delivery. Duplicate search: pur9-def-perfect-complex is a special case and the def-pod/def-pc sheaf notions are different. The blueprint node sk-def-perfect defines the same notion as a dualizable object, so I added it to blueprint.same_as, which was empty. That is the only fix, in fixes/dag/nodes/sec-six-functors/def-pod-perfect-point-complex.json. The Mathlib searches are recorded with real results and there is no match; not attaching DerivedCategory.IsPerfect is correct. No SGA is cited and no tool_uses are needed.
